propositions: The gate matches field names globally by bare attribute terminal name rather than resolving reads to their owning dataclass, so a field is incorrectly satisfied when any other unrelated config declares the same field name
CodeHealthConfig.enabled had zero read sites but passed the gate because enabled was read on UiConfig, while uniquely-named CodeHealthConfig.analyzers correctly failed the gate and required a marker
Common field names like enabled, path, timeout, remote, branch, and mode are most likely to be reused across configs and most likely to be missed by the gate

The fix must resolve each attribute read to its declaring dataclass through six patterns: section-attribute names, parameter annotations, local assignment propagation, function return annotations, conditional branches, and cross-module call-site bindings

Four fields newly flag under the fixed gate (McpConfig.readonly, McpConfig.allow_llm, McpConfig.allow_jira_sync, JiraConfig.allow_insecure) but each has a live reader via documented indirection and receives accurate read-via markers without operator triage

Existing test files must be migrated from the obsolete bare-name contract to the owner-resolution contract and must verify both that the RED-first synthetic proof holds and that required negative fixtures still pass
